mainTopic: The value of davening with the צבור and in the בית הכנסת, the readings of 'לְעֵת מְצֹא', the special place of הלכה study, and proper conduct around קריאת התורה
overview: This amud praises davening with the צבור and coming to the בית הכנסת. It opens by teaching that communal prayer is an עת רצון, and three sources are brought for this, including a ברייתא of רבי נתן. ריש לקיש warns that someone who does not enter his town's בית הכנסת is a 'bad neighbor' who brings גלות. רבי יוחנן learns that the people of בבל live long because they come early and stay late in the בית הכנסת. The גמרא then lists five readings of 'לְעֵת מְצֹא': a wife, תורה, death, burial, and a בית הכסא, and in ארץ ישראל they preferred the last. Next, רב חסדא and עולא teach that places of הלכה study are most beloved to ה׳, so אביי, רבי אמי, and רבי אסי davened where they learned. A series of teachings from עולא follows, about earning one's own living and about living near one's רבי. The amud ends with laws about not leaving during קריאת התורה, and with the duty of שנים מקרא ואחד תרגום.

steps.title: The time of communal prayer is a time of favor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the פסוק ״ואני תפלתי לך ה׳ עת רצון״. It says the עת רצון, the time of favor, is when the צבור is davening.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does the פסוק mean when it says, "But as for me, my prayer is to You, ה׳, at a time of favor"? When is a time of favor? It is the time when the congregation is praying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what a פסוק in תהלים means, then answers its own question. The 'time of favor' that דוד wanted for his תפילה is the time when the צבור davens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק implies that some times are better for תפילה than others. The גמרא identifies that special time as communal prayer. So an individual who davens together with the צבור is davening at the best possible time.

keyTerms.meaning: What is [the meaning of] what is written? This is a standard opening for explaining a פסוק.
A time of favor, a time when ה׳ is especially willing to accept תפילה
The congregation, the community praying together

steps.confusionAlert: The question ״אימתי עת רצון״ is not a challenge against anyone. The גמרא asks it only to set up its own answer: communal prayer is the time of favor.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic source in the גמרא for the special value of davening with a מנין, not only alone.

phrases.english: What is [the meaning of] that which is written:
"But as for me, my prayer is to You, ה׳,
phrases.notes: תהלים סט:יד

phrases.english: at a time of favor"?
When is a time of favor?
At the time when the congregation is praying.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion on the daf about davening in shul and with the צבור. It gives a פסוק as the source for that idea.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The time of communal prayer is an עת רצון, so תפילה with the צבור is especially accepted.

steps.title: A second source from ישעיהו
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא learns the same idea from a different פסוק: ״כה אמר ה׳ בעת רצון עניתיך״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי, son of רבי חנינא, said: we learn it from here: "So says ה׳: In a time of favor I answered you."
steps.whatsHappening: A different אמורא gives a different פסוק for the same idea. He agrees that communal prayer is special and simply brings another source for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ישעיהו‎, ה׳ is speaking to the whole nation of ישראל. So the 'time of favor' when ה׳ answers is linked to the community as a group. This makes the connection between עת רצון and the צבור even more direct.

keyTerms.meaning: From here. Used to introduce a different source for the same idea.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Chanina, said: [we learn it] from here:
"So says ה׳:
phrases.notes: ישעיהו מט:ח

phrases.english: In a time of favor I answered you."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative פסוק as the source for the same idea taught in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Communal prayer is a time of favor, learned from ״בעת רצון עניתיך״.

steps.title: A third source: ה׳ does not reject the many
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא ברבי חנינא brings two פסוקים: ״הן אל כביר ולא ימאס״ and ״פדה בשלום נפשי... כי ברבים היו עמדי״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא, son of רבי חנינא, said: we learn it from here: "Behold, God does not despise the mighty," and it is written: "He redeemed my soul in peace from the battle against me, for many were with me."
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא, the brother of רבי יוסי, brings yet another source. He combines two פסוקים to show that the תפילה of the many is never rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the first פסוק as 'God does not reject the כביר', meaning the many, the community. The second פסוק says דוד was saved because 'many were with me', meaning many people prayed together with him. Together they show that ה׳ does not turn down the תפילה of a group.

keyTerms.meaning: Mighty or great. Here it is read as 'the many', the community.
He will not despise or reject
And it is written. Introduces a second פסוק that adds to the first.

steps.confusionAlert: Read simply, ״אל כביר ולא ימאס״ seems to mean 'God is mighty and despises no one.' רבי אחא reads it differently: 'God does not despise the כביר', meaning the many.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אַחָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Acha, son of Rabbi Chanina, said: [we learn it] from here:
"Behold, God does not despise the mighty [i.e., the many]"
phrases.notes: איוב לו:ה

phrases.english: And it is written:
"He redeemed my soul in peace from the battle against me,
phrases.notes: תהלים נה:יט

phrases.english: for many were with me."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַחָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third, alternative source for the special power of communal prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ does not reject the תפילה of the many, learned from ״אל כביר ולא ימאס״ together with ״כי ברבים היו עמדי״.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי אחא's source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that a ברייתא of רבי נתן uses the same two פסוקים as רבי אחא to prove that ה׳ does not reject the תפילה of the many.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught in a ברייתא. רבי נתן says: From where do we know that הקדוש ברוך הוא does not despise the prayer of the many? As it says, "Behold, God does not despise the mighty," and it is written, "He redeemed my soul in peace from the battle against me," etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים, that says the same thing as רבי אחא. This shows that his source is backed by an earlier authority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase ״תניא נמי הכי״ means 'a ברייתא also teaches this'. רבי נתן uses exactly the same two פסוקים as רבי אחא. So רבי אחא's reading is not new; a תנא already taught it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא. This introduces support from a תנא.
From where [do we know]? Asks for a source in a פסוק.
Etc. The rest of the פסוק continues.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way [in a baraita]:
Rabbi Natan says:
From where do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not
despise the prayer of the many?
As it is stated: "Behold, God does not despise the mighty,"

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״פָּדָה בְשָׁלוֹם נַפְשִׁי מִקְּרָב לִי״ וְגוֹ׳,
phrases.english: and it is written: "He redeemed my soul in peace from the battle against me," etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 3 by showing that a ברייתא uses the same פסוקים.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אחא ברבי חנינא's source from ״הן אל כביר ולא ימאס״ and ״פדה בשלום נפשי״
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי נתן that uses the same two פסוקים

steps.title: Whoever learns, does kindness, and davens with the community redeems ה׳ and His children
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. רבי נתן reads the פסוק as ה׳ speaking: whoever learns תורה, does גמילות חסדים, and davens with the צבור is considered to have redeemed ה׳ and His children from the nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא said: Anyone who is involved in תורה, in acts of kindness, and prays with the congregation, I consider it as if he redeemed Me and My children from among the nations of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now explains the second פסוק in a new way, as if ה׳ Himself is speaking. It promises a huge reward for three things: learning תורה, doing חסד, and davening with the צבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each part of the פסוק is matched to one deed. ״בשלום״ (in peace) refers to תורה, whose ways are called peace, and the מפרשים connect חסד to peace as well. ״ברבים היו עמדי״ (many were with me) refers to davening with the צבור. ״פדה נפשי״ (he redeemed my soul) is read as ה׳ saying: this person has, so to speak, redeemed Me.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is involved in learning תורה
I consider it for him, I give him credit

steps.whatToRemember: Communal prayer is an עת רצון‎. ה׳ never rejects the תפילה of the many. Whoever combines תורה, גמילות חסדים, and davening with the צבור is considered as if he redeemed ה׳ and His children from among the nations.
steps.confusionAlert: In the simple reading, דוד is speaking about himself ('He redeemed my soul'). רבי נתן reads it as ה׳ speaking: 'he redeemed My soul.' The person who does these deeds is the redeemer, not the one being redeemed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This statement raises davening with a מנין from a good practice to something tied to the redemption of כלל ישראל and, so to speak, of the שכינה itself.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Anyone who engages in Torah [study]
and in acts of kindness
and prays with the congregation,
I credit him
as if he redeemed Me and My children
from among the nations of the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and adds a new reading of the second פסוק that teaches the great reward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning תורה, doing גמילות חסדים, and davening with the צבור is considered as if one redeemed ה׳ and His children from the nations.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Davening with the צבור, together with תורה and חסד, has a redemptive value in ה׳'s eyes.

steps.title: Skipping the local synagogue makes you a 'bad neighbor'
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש teaches that a person who has a בית הכנסת in his city but does not go in to daven is called a שכן רע, a bad neighbor.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Anyone who has a בית הכנסת in his city and does not go in there to daven is called a 'bad neighbor.' The פסוק says: 'So says ה׳: about all My bad neighbors who touch the inheritance that I gave to My people, ישראל.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a new teaching. It shows the other side of davening with the צבור: what is wrong with someone who stays away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The steps before this praised davening with the צבור. Now ריש לקיש criticizes someone who lives near a בית הכנסת and still does not go in. He reads 'touching the inheritance' as being right next to ה׳'s house without actually entering it. That makes the person a 'neighbor' of ה׳, but a bad one.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא from ארץ ישראל, the study partner of רבי יוחנן
Synagogue, the place where the צבור davens
Those who touch the inheritance, meaning they come close but do not enter

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that being close to a בית הכנסת creates a responsibility. Living nearby and not going in is treated as a real failing, not just a missed bonus.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: כָּל מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת בְּעִירוֹ,
phrases.english: Anyone who has a synagogue in his city,
and does not go in there to pray,
is called a 'bad neighbor,'
as it says: 'So says ה׳,
phrases.notes: ירמיהו יב:יד

phrases.english: about all My bad neighbors
who touch the inheritance
phrases.notes: They touch it but do not enter it. They are near the בית הכנסת and do not go in.

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר הִנְחַלְתִּי אֶת עַמִּי אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל״.
phrases.english: that I gave as an inheritance to My people Israel.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: כָּל מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת בְּעִירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of davening with the צבור, but now from the negative side: what happens to someone who stays away.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who has a בית הכנסת in his city and does not daven there is called a שכן רע.

steps.title: He also brings exile on himself and his children
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש adds that this person also causes גלות for himself and his children, based on the rest of the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And more than that: he causes exile for himself and his children. The פסוק says: 'Behold, I will uproot them from their land, and I will uproot the house of יהודה from among them.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש continues his teaching and adds a second, harsher result. This person does not only get a bad name; he also brings exile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ולא עוד אלא' tell us a new point is being added on top of the first. The proof comes from the end of the same פסוק in ירמיהו, which describes uprooting the people from their land.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but also...

phrases.english: And not only that, but
he causes exile for himself and his children,
as it says: 'Behold, I will uproot them from upon their land,
and the house of Judah I will uproot from among them.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא שֶׁגּוֹרֵם גָּלוּת לוֹ וּלְבָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further consequence to ריש לקיש's teaching from step 6, using the rest of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not going to the בית הכנסת causes גלות for the person and his children.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is surprised that people in בבל live long
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן hears that there are old people in בבל. He is surprised, because the פסוק promises long life 'on the land,' meaning ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told רבי יוחנן: 'There are old people in בבל.' He was amazed and said: 'It is written, "So that your days and the days of your children will be many on the land." But outside the land, no!'
steps.whatsHappening: A story begins. רבי יוחנן raises a difficulty: a פסוק seems to show that long life comes only in ארץ ישראל, so how can there be old people in בבל?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question mark here is not a request for information; it works as a challenge. רבי יוחנן reads 'על האדמה' as limiting the promise of long life to ארץ ישראל. So the fact that people in בבל live long seems to contradict the פסוק, and something must explain it.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not denying that the old people exist. He accepts the report and is asking how it fits with the פסוק.

phrases.english: They said to Rabbi Yochanan:
There are old people in Babylonia.
He was amazed and said:
'So that your days will be many
phrases.notes: דברים יא:כא

phrases.english: and the days of your children, on the land,' is written,
but outside the Land, no?
phrases.notes: The promise seems to apply only in ארץ ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּמַהּ וַאֲמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story that leads into the reward for going to the בית הכנסת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reality that people in בבל live long lives
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק promises long life 'על האדמה,' which means only in ארץ ישראל, so long life in בבל seems unexplained.

steps.title: Going early and late to shul is what helps them
steps.stepSummary: When רבי יוחנן hears that the people of בבל come early and stay late in the בית הכנסת, he says this is what gives them long life.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they told him that they come early and stay late in the בית הכנסת, he said: 'That is what helps them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The difficulty is answered. The people of בבל earn long life through their dedication to the בית הכנסת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being in ארץ ישראל is one way to earn long life, but it is not the only one. Coming early and staying late in the בית הכנסת earns the same blessing even in חוץ לארץ.

keyTerms.meaning: They come early (morning) and stay late (evening)
That is what helped them / was effective for them

phrases.english: Once they told him
that they come early and stay late at the synagogue,
he said: That is what helps them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְאָמְרִי לֵיהּ מְקַדְּמִי וּמְחַשְּׁכִי לְבֵי כְנִישְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves רבי יוחנן's surprise from step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a different cause of long life
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Long life comes only from living in ארץ ישראל.
steps.terutzMaskana: Coming early and staying late in the בית הכנסת also brings long life, even outside ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי's advice to his sons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the idea with רבי יהושע בן לוי's advice to his sons: go early and late to the בית הכנסת so that you will live long.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יהושע בן לוי said to his sons: 'Come early, stay late, and go into the בית הכנסת, so that your lives will be long.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רבי יוחנן's answer. Another אמורא gave the same advice to his own children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'דאמר' ('as he said') connects this to the previous step as backing. רבי יהושע בן לוי directly links going early and late to the בית הכנסת with a longer life, the same link רבי יוחנן made.

keyTerms.meaning: An early אמורא in ארץ ישראל
So that your lives will be lengthened

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי לִבְנֵיהּ:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said to his sons:
Come early and stay late
and go into the synagogue,
so that your lives will be lengthened.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי לִבְנֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That going early and late to the בית הכנסת brings long life
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע בן לוי's instruction to his sons

steps.title: The verse behind the reward of long life
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא ברבי חנינא gives the פסוק source: 'Fortunate is the man who listens to Me, watching at My doors every day,' followed by 'for whoever finds Me finds life.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא ברבי חנינא said: What is the פסוק? 'Fortunate is the person who listens to Me, watching at My doors day after day, guarding the doorposts of My entrances.' And right after it is written: 'For whoever finds Me finds life.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives a פסוק as the source for the idea that the בית הכנסת brings long life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק describes someone who waits at ה׳'s doors every day; the בית הכנסת is read as ה׳'s house. The next פסוק gives the reward, which is 'life.' Together they tie dedication to the בית הכנסת to long life.

keyTerms.meaning: To watch diligently at My doors
And it is written after it

steps.whyThisMatters: The plural 'doorposts' and 'entrances' in this פסוק sets up רב חסדא's teaching about 'two doorways' in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Acha son of Rabbi Chanina said:
What is the verse?
'Fortunate is the man who listens to Me,
phrases.notes: משלי ח:לד

phrases.english: watching at My doors day by day,
guarding the doorposts of My entrances,'
and it is written after it:
'For whoever finds Me finds life.'
phrases.notes: משלי ח:לה

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק source for רבי יהושע בן לוי's advice in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That going to the בית הכנסת brings long life

steps.title: רב חסדא: enter two doorways into the בית הכנסת
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says a person should always enter 'two doorways' into the בית הכנסת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: A person should always enter two doorways into the בית הכנסת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a practical rule based on the 'doors' and 'doorposts' in the פסוק. The wording is unclear, and the גמרא will question it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural words in the פסוק ('My doors', 'My entrances') suggest more than one doorway. רב חסדא turns this into practical guidance about how far into the בית הכנסת a person should go.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
A person should always enter
two doorways into the synagogue.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לְעוֹלָם יִכָּנֵס אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a practical rule on the plural wording of the פסוק in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should enter 'two doorways' into the בית הכנסת.

steps.title: Can it really mean two literal doors?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges reading רב חסדא literally: does he really mean one must pass through two actual doors?
steps.simpleTranslation: Two doorways? Could you really think that?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the plain meaning of רב חסדא's words. Reading them literally does not make sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'סלקא דעתך' means 'would it enter your mind?' The literal reading is a problem because many places of davening have only one door. A rule that requires two real doors cannot be what רב חסדא meant.

keyTerms.meaning: Would it enter your mind? (rejects a reading as unreasonable)

phrases.english: Two doorways, would that enter your mind?!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵי פְתָחִים סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רב חסדא in step 12.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Requiring two actual doors is unreasonable, since a בית הכנסת may have only one door.

steps.title: It means walk in the length of two doorways, then daven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the reading: רב חסדא meant a person should go in a distance equal to two doorways, and then daven.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: the distance of two doorways, and after that he should daven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading רב חסדא's words differently. 'Two doorways' is a measurement of distance, not a count of doors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אלא אימא' changes how we read the statement. A person should go into the בית הכנסת at least the width of two doorways (about eight טפחים) before davening, instead of staying by the entrance. This also fits the plural 'doorposts' in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (read it this way instead)

steps.whatToRemember: Going to the בית הכנסת matters a great deal. Someone who skips it is a 'bad neighbor' and brings גלות, while someone who comes early and stays late earns long life even in חוץ לארץ. When you come in, go a real distance inside (the length of two doorways) before you daven, and do not stay at the door.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Two doorways' does NOT mean walking through two doors. It is a measurement: go in as far as the width of two doorways.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
the distance of two doorways,
phrases.notes: Commonly explained as about eight טפחים (four per doorway).

phrases.english: and after that he should pray.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא, שִׁיעוּר שְׁנֵי פְתָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 13 by reinterpreting רב חסדא's words.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא meant passing through two physical doors.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant going inside a distance equal to two doorways before davening.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One should walk into the בית הכנסת at least the length of two doorways before davening.

steps.title: The time of finding means finding a wife
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא explains that 'לְעֵת מְצֹא' in תהלים refers to finding a wife. He proves it from the פסוק 'מָצָא אִשָּׁה מָצָא טוֹב'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For this, let every pious man pray to You in the time of finding.' רבי חנינא said: 'The time of finding' means a wife, as it says: 'He who finds a wife finds good.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new פסוק that uses the word 'finding' and asks what a pious person prays for at the 'time of finding.' רבי חנינא gives the first answer: a wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in תהלים never says what is being 'found.' רבי חנינא fills in the gap by linking the same root מצא to משלי, where 'finding' clearly means finding a wife. So a חסיד should daven to find the right spouse.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time of finding: the unclear phrase being explained
He who finds a wife finds good (משלי)

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a list of opinions on one phrase. Each opinion names a different major 'find' in life that is worth davening about.

phrases.english: "For this, let every pious man pray
phrases.notes: תהלים לב:ו

phrases.english: to You in the time of finding,"
phrases.notes: The phrase that needs explaining

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
"In the time of finding": this is a wife,
as it is said: "He who finds a wife finds good."
phrases.notes: משלי יח:כב, linked by the shared word מצא

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: לְעֵת מְצֹא זוֹ אִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 11 quoted 'כִּי מֹצְאִי מָצָא חַיִּים'. That 'finding' word leads the גמרא to explain another 'finding' פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לְעֵת מְצֹא' refers to finding a wife, based on the shared word מצא in משלי.

steps.title: The wedding custom in ארץ ישראל: 'מָצָא' or 'מוֹצֵא'?
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל, people would ask a new groom 'מָצָא או מוֹצֵא?' They meant: is your wife like the good פסוק in משלי, or like the bitter פסוק in קהלת?
steps.simpleTranslation: In ארץ ישראל, when a man married a woman, they would ask him: 'מָצָא or מוֹצֵא?' 'מָצָא' as written: 'He who finds a wife finds good and obtains favor from ה׳‎.' 'מוֹצֵא' as written: 'And I find the woman more bitter than death.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a side note that builds on רבי חנינא's idea of 'finding a wife.' It describes a wedding custom that played on two פסוקים about 'finding' a wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים use the root מצא about a wife, but they say opposite things. One says she is good, and the other says she is bitter. The question asked the groom, half in jest, which kind of 'find' he had made.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל (west of בבל)
Matza or Motzei? The two 'finding' פסוקים

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new explanation of 'לְעֵת מְצֹא.' It is a side note that adds to רבי חנינא's 'wife' reading. The list of opinions picks up again in the next step.

phrases.english: In the West (Eretz Yisrael), when a man married a woman,
they would say to him like this:
"Matza" or "Motzei"?
phrases.notes: Which פסוק fits your wife?

phrases.english: "Matza," as it is written: "He who finds a wife finds good
and obtains favor from ה׳,"
"Motzei," as it is written:
"And I find more bitter than death
the woman," etc.
phrases.notes: קהלת ז:כו

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַעְרְבָא כִּי נָסֵיב אִינָשׁ אִתְּתָא אָמְרִי לֵיהּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This builds on רבי חנינא's 'wife' reading with a related custom that uses two 'finding' פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ארץ ישראל, people asked a groom whether his marriage fit 'מָצָא' (good) or 'מוֹצֵא' (bitter).

steps.title: The time of finding means finding תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן disagrees and says 'לְעֵת מְצֹא' means תורה. He brings the פסוק 'כִּי מֹצְאִי מָצָא חַיִּים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן says: 'The time of finding' means תורה, as it says: 'For whoever finds Me finds life.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second explanation of 'לְעֵת מְצֹא.' רבי נתן says the pious person prays about finding תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן uses the same method as רבי חנינא, matching the word מצא in another פסוק. He uses the משלי פסוק about תורה, the same one quoted in step 11. In that פסוק, 'finding Me' means finding תורה, and that brings life.

keyTerms.meaning: Torah: what is being 'found' in רבי נתן's view
Whoever finds Me finds life (משלי ח:לה)

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says:
"In the time of finding": this is Torah,
as it is said: "For whoever finds Me finds life," etc.
phrases.notes: The same פסוק quoted in step 11

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר: לְעֵת מְצֹא זוֹ תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a different reading of the same phrase that רבי חנינא explained in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לְעֵת מְצֹא' refers to finding Torah.

steps.title: The time of finding means death
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says 'לְעֵת מְצֹא' means death. He uses the פסוק 'לַמָּוֶת תּוֹצָאוֹת', which has a similar-sounding word.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: 'The time of finding' means death, as it says: 'The ways out (תּוֹצָאוֹת) of death.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third explanation. רב נחמן בר יצחק says a pious person prays about the time of death, that he should leave the world in peace.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן בר יצחק links 'מְצֹא' to 'תּוֹצָאוֹת' because the two words sound alike. That gives a different meaning: the 'time of finding' is the moment a person goes out of this world. Steps 19-20 support this reading, and the list of opinions continues in steps 21 and 24.

keyTerms.meaning: The ways out of death (תהלים סח:כא)

steps.confusionAlert: תּוֹצָאוֹת does not come from the same root as מְצֹא. The link is based on how similar the two words sound, which is looser than the earlier matches.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
"In the time of finding": this is death,
as it is said: "The ways out of death."
phrases.notes: תּוֹצָאוֹת sounds like מְצֹא

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר לְעֵת מְצֹא זוֹ מִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a third reading of 'לְעֵת מְצֹא,' after the wife reading (step 15) and the Torah reading (step 17).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לְעֵת מְצֹא' refers to death: one should pray for a peaceful passing.

steps.title: A ברייתא backs up the death reading: 903 kinds of death
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רב נחמן בר יצחק. It teaches that 903 kinds of death were created, because the word 'תּוֹצָאוֹת' adds up to 903 in גימטריא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: 903 kinds of death were created in the world. The פסוק says 'לַמָּוֶת תּוֹצָאוֹת' ('the ways out to death'), and the word 'תּוֹצָאוֹת' equals 903 in גימטריא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב נחמן בר יצחק, who said 'לְעֵת מְצֹא' means death. It uses the same פסוק he used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן בר יצחק linked 'מְצֹא' to 'תּוֹצָאוֹת' in the פסוק about death. This ברייתא shows that the same פסוק was already used by a תנא to teach about the many kinds of death. Since there are so many ways to die, a person should pray to die in an easy way.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא that supports what was just said)
Counting the number value of Hebrew letters

phrases.english: It was also taught this way (in a baraita):
Nine hundred and three kinds of death
were created in the world,
as it says: "The ways out to death,"
and "totzaot" in gematria adds up to this (903).

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 18 (רב נחמן בר יצחק's death reading) with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim that 'לְעֵת מְצֹא' refers to death
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that uses 'לַמָּוֶת תּוֹצָאוֹת' to count 903 kinds of death

steps.title: The hardest death and the easiest death
steps.stepSummary: Of all the kinds of death, אסכרא (croup) is the hardest and נשיקה (the 'kiss') is the easiest. The גמרא gives a picture for each one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The hardest of all deaths is אסכרא, and the easiest of all is נשיקה. אסכרא is like a thorn stuck in tangled wool that is pulled out backward. Some say it is like ropes being pulled through the opening of the throat. נשיקה is like pulling a hair out of milk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes the two ends of the list of 903 deaths: the most painful one and the gentlest one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thorn pulled backward through wool rips and tears everything around it. Ropes in the throat are almost impossible to bear. A hair slides out of milk smoothly, with nothing pulling on it. This shows what a person is praying for: to leave the world gently, not painfully.

keyTerms.meaning: Croup, a painful choking disease of the throat; the hardest death
Like pulling a hair out of milk

phrases.english: The hardest of them all is croup (askara),
the easiest of them all is the kiss (neshikah).
Croup is like a thorn
stuck in a tangle of wool
that is pulled out backward,
and some say
it is like ropes at the opening of the throat;
the kiss is like
pulling a hair out of milk.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָשָׁה שֶׁבְּכֻלָּן אַסְכָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the ברייתא of Step 19 by describing the two extremes of the 903 deaths.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אסכרא is the most painful death and נשיקה is the gentlest.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: 'לעת מצא' means burial
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives another explanation: 'לְעֵת מְצֹא' refers to burial.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: 'At the time of finding' means burial.
steps.whatsHappening: A new explanation of the פסוק: רבי יוחנן says a חסיד prays to merit a proper burial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier views said the 'finding' is a wife, תורה, or death. רבי יוחנן moves one step past death to what happens afterward. He says a person should pray to be buried properly and with respect.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
"At the time of finding" – this is burial.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another explanation of 'לְעֵת מְצֹא', alongside the explanations in Steps 15–18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לְעֵת מְצֹא' refers to meriting a proper burial.

steps.title: רבי חנינא brings a פסוק for the burial reading
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא supports רבי יוחנן with a פסוק from איוב: people 'rejoice when they find a grave.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: What is the פסוק that shows this? 'Those who rejoice with joy, and are glad when they find a grave.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא gives a source for רבי יוחנן's idea. The פסוק in איוב uses the same word 'finding' (ימצאו) for a grave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works by matching words. 'מְצֹא' in תהלים is explained by 'יִמְצְאוּ קָבֶר' in איוב. Finding a grave can be a reason for joy, which shows it is something worth praying for.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the פסוק (that is the source)?

steps.confusionAlert: This רבי חנינא is not disagreeing with רבי יוחנן or repeating his own earlier view (a wife, Step 15). Here he is simply giving a source for רבי יוחנן's explanation.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said: What is the verse?
"Those who rejoice with joy,
and are glad when they find a grave."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא מַאי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the פסוק that supports רבי יוחנן's reading in Step 21.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's reading that 'לְעֵת מְצֹא' means burial

steps.title: A popular saying: pray until the last shovelful of earth
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב שילא connects the burial reading to a common saying: a person should pray for mercy until the very last shovelful of earth is thrown on his grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב שילא said: This is what people mean when they say, 'A person should pray for mercy even until the last shovelful of earth, so that there is peace.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב שילא shows that an everyday saying matches רבי יוחנן's idea. People should keep praying all the way through their burial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying adds a new point: praying does not stop at death. Until the grave is fully closed, a person still needs ה׳'s mercy for a proper, peaceful burial. That is exactly what רבי יוחנן said the חסיד prays for.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what people say (a popular saying that matches the idea)

steps.whatToRemember: The burial explanation (רבי יוחנן) has two supports: a פסוק in איוב and a popular saying. A person should pray for a proper burial.

phrases.english: Rabbah bar Rav Sheila said:
This is what people say:
A person should ask for mercy
even until the last shovelful of earth, (for) peace.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ דְּאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a popular saying as more support for the burial reading.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that one should pray for a proper burial
steps.raayaSupportSource: A popular saying about praying until the last shovelful of earth

steps.title: מר זוטרא: 'לעת מצא' means a בית הכסא
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא gives a surprising explanation: 'לְעֵת מְצֹא' refers to finding a בית הכסא (a place to relieve oneself).
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: 'At the time of finding' means a בית הכסא.
steps.whatsHappening: Another explanation: מר זוטרא says a person should pray to find a decent place to relieve himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In their times there were no bathrooms inside houses, and people often had to go out of town to a field. Finding a proper, nearby place was hard and a real need. So it is something a person would pray for.

keyTerms.meaning: A bathroom, a place to relieve oneself

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
"At the time of finding" – this is the lavatory.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר זוּטְרָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers yet another explanation of 'לְעֵת מְצֹא', after the burial reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לְעֵת מְצֹא' refers to finding a proper בית הכסא.

steps.title: In ארץ ישראל they said מר זוטרא's explanation is the best
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of ארץ ישראל say מר זוטרא's explanation is better than all the others.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West (ארץ ישראל) they said: The explanation of מר זוטרא is better than all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The list of explanations ends with a judgment. In ארץ ישראל they preferred מר זוטרא's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some commentaries explain that 'מוֹצָאוֹת' is used in תנ״ך for a place of waste (מלכים ב 10:27). That makes the בית הכסא reading the closest match to the words. This closes the whole section on 'לְעֵת מְצֹא'.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: There are five explanations of 'לְעֵת מְצֹא': a wife (רבי חנינא), תורה (רבי נתן), death (רב נחמן בר יצחק), burial (רבי יוחנן), and a בית הכסא (מר זוטרא). The ברייתא about 903 deaths is not a separate explanation; it supports the death reading. In ארץ ישראל they considered מר זוטרא's (בית הכסא) the best.

phrases.english: They say in the West (Eretz Yisrael):
This (explanation) of Mar Zutra is better than all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי בְּמַעְרְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Judges between all the explanations given so far and prefers Step 24.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מר זוטרא's explanation (finding a בית הכסא) is considered the best reading of 'לְעֵת מְצֹא'.

steps.title: רבא asks to hear רב חסדא's teachings about the בית הכנסת
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רפרם בר פפא to share the fine teachings he said in the name of רב חסדא about the בית הכנסת. This brings the גמרא back to its main topic.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רפרם בר פפא: Please tell us some of those excellent teachings that you said in the name of רב חסדא about matters of the בית הכנסת.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבא makes a request, and the answer will come in the next part of the גמרא. It moves us back from the side topic to the topic of תפילה and the בית הכנסת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'לְעֵת מְצֹא' discussion was a side branch. It started from the פסוק about what a חסיד prays for. Now the גמרא returns to the main subject, starting a new set of רב חסדא's teachings that רפרם בר פפא will report.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rava said to Rafram bar Pappa:
Let the master tell us
some of those excellent teachings
that you said in the name of Rav Chisda
about matters of the synagogue.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא לֵימָא לָן מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the 'לְעֵת מְצֹא' side topic and returns to teachings of רב חסדא about the בית הכנסת (compare רב חסדא's statement in Step 12).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רב חסדא's teachings about the בית הכנסת, as reported by רפרם בר פפא

steps.title: רב חסדא: ה׳ loves the gates distinguished in הלכה
steps.stepSummary: רפרם reports רב חסדא's reading of a פסוק in תהלים. 'שערי ציון' means gates that are 'מצוינים' (distinguished) through הלכה, and ה׳ loves them more than בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רב חסדא said. What is the meaning of the verse 'ה׳ loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob'? ה׳ loves the gates that are distinguished in הלכה more than synagogues and study halls.
steps.whatsHappening: רפרם answers רבא's question from the last step. He shares one of רב חסדא's teachings about the בית הכנסת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא reads 'ציון' as if it said 'מצוין', meaning outstanding or distinguished. The 'gates of Zion' become places that stand out through deep הלכה learning. These are ranked even above the 'dwellings of Jacob', which he reads as ordinary בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written? (opens an explanation of a פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: 'צִיּוֹן' here is not about the place called Zion. רב חסדא is making a wordplay with 'מְצוּיָּנִים' (distinguished). Also, he is not saying synagogues are unimportant. He is saying that places of הלכה are loved even more.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: He (Rafram) said to him: This is what Rav Chisda said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"The Lord loves the gates of Zion
phrases.notes: תהלים פז:ב

phrases.english: more than all the dwellings of Jacob"
The Lord loves the gates that are distinguished in halacha
phrases.notes: צִיּוֹן is read as מְצוּיָּנִים

phrases.english: more than synagogues and study halls.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's request for רב חסדא's teachings about the בית הכנסת.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ה׳ loves places distinguished in הלכה more than בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות, based on reading ציון as מצוין.

steps.title: עולא: after the חורבן, ה׳ has only the four אמות of הלכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא links רב חסדא's teaching to עולא's statement. Since the בית המקדש was destroyed, ה׳ has nothing in His world except the four אמות of הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what רבי חייא בר אמי said in the name of עולא: From the day the בית המקדש was destroyed, הקדוש ברוך הוא has nothing in His world except the four אמות of הלכה alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a well-known statement that matches רב חסדא's idea. It shows that the same idea appears elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'והיינו דאמר' means 'this is the same idea as what so-and-so said.' עולא explains why places of הלכה are so beloved. Once the בית המקדש is gone, the place where ה׳'s presence is most found is wherever הלכה is being learned.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what [so-and-so] said (shows the same idea in another teaching)
The four cubits (personal space) of הלכה study

steps.whyThisMatters: This is one of the most famous lines in ש״ס about the value of learning הלכה. The next two steps build on it in actual practice.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא:
phrases.english: And this is what Rabbi Chiyya bar Ami said in the name of Ulla:
From the day that the Temple was destroyed,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לוֹ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעוֹלָמוֹ
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, has nothing in His world

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁל הֲלָכָה בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: except the four cubits of halacha alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב חסדא's teaching with a parallel statement from עולא.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's claim that places of הלכה are especially beloved to ה׳.
steps.raayaSupportSource: עולא's statement, reported by רבי חייא בר אמי, that after the חורבן ה׳ has only the four אמות of הלכה.

steps.title: אביי begins davening only where he learns
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports how he changed his practice. He used to learn at home and daven in the בית הכנסת. After hearing עולא's teaching, he davened only in the place where he learned.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: At first I used to learn at home and daven in the בית הכנסת. Once I heard what רבי חייא בר אמי said in the name of עולא, that since the בית המקדש was destroyed ה׳ has only the four אמות of הלכה, I davened only where I learned.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי shows how עולא's teaching changed what he actually did. It is a practical application of the idea from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי understood עולא literally and practically. If the place of הלכה is where ה׳'s presence is found, then that is the best place to daven. So he moved his davening into his place of learning.

keyTerms.meaning: I would learn / review my studies

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא repeats עולא's statement word for word. It is not a new teaching. אביי is quoting it to explain why he changed his practice.

phrases.english: And Abaye said:
At first I used to learn inside the house
and I would pray in the synagogue.
Once I heard this

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא —
phrases.english: that Rabbi Chiyya bar Ami said in the name of Ulla:
From the day that the Temple was destroyed,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לוֹ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעוֹלָמוֹ
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, has nothing in His world

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁל הֲלָכָה בִּלְבַד —
phrases.english: except the four cubits of halacha alone —

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲוָה מְצַלֵּינָא אֶלָּא הֵיכָא דְּגָרֵיסְנָא.
phrases.english: I would pray only where I learned.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מֵרֵישׁ הֲוָה גָּרֵיסְנָא בְּגוֹ בֵּיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies עולא's statement in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of the special status of the four אמות of הלכה, אביי davened only in the place where he learned.

steps.title: רבי אמי and רבי אסי daven between the pillars where they learn
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי and רבי אסי had thirteen בתי כנסיות in טבריא. Even so, they davened only between the pillars of the place where they learned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי and רבי אסי had thirteen synagogues in טבריא. Even so, they davened only between the pillars, in the place where they learned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second example of great אמוראים who davened where they learned. It wraps up the section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The detail of 'thirteen synagogues' makes the point stronger. They had plenty of synagogues to choose from and still chose their place of learning. This shows that אביי's practice was not a one-time oddity. Other great רבנים did the same.

keyTerms.meaning: טבריא (Tiberias), a major Torah center in ארץ ישראל
Between the pillars (of the study hall)

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא and עולא teach that places of הלכה study hold a unique holiness, especially after the חורבן. אביי, רבי אמי, and רבי אסי acted on this by davening where they learned.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi,
even though they had
thirteen synagogues in Tiberias,
would pray only between the pillars,
where they would learn.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי אַף עַל גַּב דַּהֲווֹ לְהוּ תְּלֵיסַר בֵּי כְנִישְׁתָּא בִּטְבֶרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another example of the same practice as אביי.
steps.raayaObject: The practice of davening in one's place of הלכה study, based on עולא's teaching.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The conduct of רבי אמי and רבי אסי in טבריא.

steps.title: One who lives from his own work is greater than a God-fearing person
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אמי, in the name of עולא, says that one who benefits from his own hard work is greater than a ירא שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא בר אמי said in the name of עולא: A person who enjoys the fruits of his own hard work is greater than a God-fearing person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from the same pair, רבי חייא בר אמי quoting עולא. It praises a person who supports himself from his own work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'ירא שמים' here is a person so caught up in his fear of Heaven that he does not work and relies on others. The claim is a comparison: earning your own living with יראת שמים ranks higher. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: One who benefits from his own hard work

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying that fearing Heaven is bad. It means that a person who fears Heaven and also works for his living is greater than one who fears Heaven but does not support himself.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiya bar Ami said in the name of Ulla:
phrases.notes: The word 'And' signals a continuing series of teachings from the same speaker.

phrases.english: Greater is one who benefits from his own labor
than a God-fearing person,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new teaching in the series of statements from רבי חייא בר אמי in the name of עולא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who supports himself from his own labor is greater than a ירא שמים who does not.

steps.title: Proof from the verses: 'and it is good for you' is written only about the worker
steps.stepSummary: The proof compares two פסוקים in תהלים. The God-fearing man gets only 'אשרי', while the one who eats from his labor gets both 'אשריך' (this world) and 'וטוב לך' (עולם הבא).
steps.simpleTranslation: About a God-fearing person it is written, 'Happy is the man who fears ה׳.' But about one who lives from his own work it is written, 'When you eat the labor of your hands, you are happy and it is good for you.' 'You are happy' means in this world. 'And it is good for you' means in the World to Come. About the God-fearing person, 'and it is good for you' is not written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the previous statement by comparing what the פסוקים say about each person. The worker gets an extra blessing that the God-fearing person does not get.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both people are called 'happy' (אשרי). Only the worker gets the extra words 'וטוב לך', which are read as reward in עולם הבא. One extra blessing means a greater level, and that proves the claim in step 31.

phrases.english: For regarding a God-fearing person it is written:
"Happy is the man who fears the Lord"
phrases.notes: תהלים קיב:א

phrases.english: while regarding one who benefits from his labor it is written:
"When you eat the labor of your hands,
phrases.notes: תהלים קכח:ב

phrases.english: you are happy and it is good for you."
"You are happy" means in this world;
"and it is good for you" means in the World to Come.
But regarding a God-fearing person,
"and it is good for you" is not written about him.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִילּוּ גַּבֵּי יְרֵא שָׁמַיִם כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural proof for the statement in step 31.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that one who benefits from his labor is greater than a ירא שמים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים קיב:א compared with תהלים קכח:ב. Only the second verse adds 'וטוב לך', which is read as reward in עולם הבא.
steps.whatToRemember: Earning your own living earns 'אשריך' in this world and 'וטוב לך' in עולם הבא. The words 'וטוב לך' are not written about the God-fearing person who does not work.

steps.title: A person should always live in the place of his teacher
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אמי, in the name of עולא, teaches that a person should always live in the same place as his רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא בר אמי said in the name of עולא: A person should always live in the place where his teacher lives.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching from the same speaker. He advises a person to live near his רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the רבי's presence keeps the student away from sin. The next step proves this with a story from שלמה המלך.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiya bar Ami said in the name of Ulla:
A person should always live in the place of his teacher,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate teaching in the same series.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should always live where his רבי lives.

steps.title: Proof from שלמה and שמעי בן גרא
steps.stepSummary: As long as שמעי בן גרא (by tradition שלמה's teacher) was alive, שלמה did not marry בת פרעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For as long as שמעי בן גרא was alive, שלמה did not marry Pharaoh's daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that living near your רבי protects you. It points to שלמה, who did not do this wrong while his teacher was alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By tradition, שמעי בן גרא was שלמה's teacher. In מלכים א, שמעי's death is told at the end of chapter 2, and שלמה's marriage to בת פרעה comes right after, at the start of chapter 3. That order shows the teacher's presence had held him back.

keyTerms.meaning: A great scholar who, by tradition, was שלמה's teacher

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכָּל זְמַן שֶׁשִּׁמְעִי בֶּן גֵּרָא קַיָּים,
phrases.english: for as long as Shimi ben Gera was alive,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נָשָׂא שְׁלֹמֹה אֶת בַּת פַּרְעֹה.
phrases.english: Solomon did not marry Pharaoh's daughter.
phrases.notes: In מלכים א, שמעי dies at the end of chapter 2, and the marriage is told at the start of chapter 3.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁכָּל זְמַן שֶׁשִּׁמְעִי בֶּן גֵּרָא קַיָּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the teaching of step 33 with an example from Tanach.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one should live in his רבי's place.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The order of events in מלכים א: שמעי's death is followed right away by שלמה marrying בת פרעה.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the opposite: do not live there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the teaching with a ברייתא that says a person should NOT live in his רבי's place.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: A person should not live in the place of his teacher!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction. A ברייתא gives the exact opposite advice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא says 'live there,' and the ברייתא says 'do not live there.' Both cannot be true as stated, so the גמרא needs a way to reconcile them. The answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught (in a ברייתא)? This introduces a contradicting source.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: one should not live there!
phrases.notes: That is, a person should not live in his teacher's place.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the teaching of step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's rule that one should live in his רבי's place.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא directly states the opposite rule.

steps.title: It depends on whether the student accepts his teacher's authority
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction. A student who submits to his רבי should live near him. A student who does not submit should not live near him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This teaching, that he should live there, is about a student who submits to his teacher. That teaching, that he should not, is about a student who does not submit to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by applying each source to a different kind of student.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the student accepts his רבי's guidance, living nearby keeps him from sin, as with שלמה. If he does not accept it, living nearby only leads to fighting and disrespect, so it is better to live elsewhere. Both sources are true, each in its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (no real contradiction)
This one ... that one (assigning each source its own case)

steps.whatToRemember: Live near your רבי if you will listen to him. If you will not, living near him leads to conflict, so stay away.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where he submits to him,
that is where he does not submit to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא דִּכְיִיף לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 35.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source applies to a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources seemed to give opposite rules for the same situation.
steps.terutzMaskana: עולא's rule is for a student who submits to his רבי. The ברייתא is for a student who does not.

steps.title: Walking out on the open ספר תורה is forsaking ה׳
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי teaches that 'those who forsake ה׳ will perish' refers to someone who leaves the ספר תורה and walks out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה said in the name of רבי מנחם, who said in the name of רבי אמי: What does the פסוק 'Those who forsake ה׳ will perish' mean? It is talking about a person who leaves the ספר תורה and goes out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching. It explains a פסוק in ישעיה as a warning against walking out of the בית כנסת while the ספר תורה is being read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'forsaking ה׳' are applied to a concrete act: getting up and leaving while the ספר תורה is open. Walking out at that moment looks like running away from ה׳'s word. This sets up the practical questions in the next steps about when, if ever, a person may leave.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written? (opens an explanation of a פסוק)
Those who forsake ה׳ will perish (ישעיה א:כח)
One who leaves the Torah scroll behind
And goes out (of the בית כנסת)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the הלכה that a person may not leave the בית כנסת during קריאת התורה.

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yehuda said,
Rabbi Menachem said,
Rabbi Ami said:
What is meant by what is written: 'Those who forsake ה׳ will perish'?
This is one who leaves the Torah scroll and goes out.
phrases.notes: Meaning: while it is open and being read.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה, אָמַר רַבִּי מְנַחֵם, אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching that returns to the general topic of the בית כנסת, after the discussion of living near one's רבי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leaving the בית כנסת while the ספר תורה is being read is 'forsaking ה׳' and is forbidden.

steps.title: רבי אבהו left only between one reader and the next
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו's practice was to go out only during the break between two people reading from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו would go out between one man and the next man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how a great אמורא put the previous teaching into practice. It describes when רבי אבהו allowed himself to leave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Between one עולה and the next, the reading has stopped and the scroll is not being actively read. Leaving then does not look like walking out on the תורה. This narrows רבי אמי's prohibition: the problem is leaving during the reading itself, not during a real break.

keyTerms.meaning: Between one man (reader) and the next

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אבהו is not disagreeing with רבי אמי. He accepts the prohibition and shows that the break between readers does not count as 'forsaking'.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu would go out
between one man and the next man.
phrases.notes: Between one person reading from the Torah and the next.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ נָפֵיק בֵּין גַּבְרָא לְגַבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the prohibition in Step 37 works in practice and points to a permitted window.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person may leave in the break between one Torah reader and the next.

steps.title: Is the break between two verses also allowed?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks whether a person may leave in the short pause between one פסוק and the next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: What is the law about leaving between one פסוק and the next?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks a follow-up question that builds on רבי אבהו's practice. He wants to know whether a smaller pause also counts as a break.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Between readers there is a full stop. Between פסוקים there is only a short pause (in their time, for the תרגום translation), and the same reader is still in the middle of his reading. The question is whether that pause is enough of a break to allow leaving.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked (raises a question that has no clear answer yet)
Between one verse and the next

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
Between one verse and the next verse, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבי אבהו's permitted window and asks whether a smaller pause qualifies.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the pause between פסוקים count as a break that allows leaving, like the break between readers?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: No answer is found, so רב פפא's question is left standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand. The question remains unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion by saying it has no answer to רב פפא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תיקו' means the question stays open. The גמרא itself gives no ruling. In practice, the שולחן ערוך permits leaving only between readers, as רבי אבהו did, and not between פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: Walking out during קריאת התורה is 'forsaking ה׳'. Leaving between two readers is allowed (רבי אבהו). Leaving between two פסוקים is an unresolved doubt (תיקו), so it is best avoided.
steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the answer is 'no'. It means the גמרא could not decide, so in practice we act with caution.

phrases.english: Let it stand (unresolved).

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּיקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רב פפא's question without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether one may leave between פסוקים is left as an unresolved doubt. In practice, the פוסקים permit leaving only between readers.

steps.title: רב ששת turns away from the Torah reading to learn
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת would turn his face away from the ספר תורה during the reading and learn. He explained: we are busy with our learning, and they are busy with theirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת would turn his face away and learn. He said: We are busy with ours, and they are busy with theirs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about how רב ששת acted during קריאת התורה. It shows a case that seems to clash with the warning against leaving the ספר תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי said that someone who walks away from the ספר תורה falls under 'those who forsake ה׳‎.' רב ששת did not leave. He stayed but turned away to learn תורה שבעל פה, while the others listened to תורה שבכתב. His point is that he was not abandoning תורה, because he was busy with a different part of תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: He would turn his face away
He studies or reviews his learning
We are busy with ours (our learning)
They are busy with theirs (listening to the reading)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב ששת was ignoring Torah or walking out. He stayed in place and was learning Torah himself. That is exactly why the warning of 'those who forsake ה׳' does not apply to him.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet would turn his face away and study.
phrases.notes: He turned away from the ספר תורה while it was being read.

phrases.english: He said: We are busy with ours,
phrases.notes: Our learning, meaning the Oral Torah.

phrases.english: and they are busy with theirs.
phrases.notes: The congregation is listening to the Written Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מַהְדַּר אַפֵּיהּ וְגָרֵיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the practice of רבי אבהו and the unresolved question of רב פפא about when one may leave, this story shows a related case: staying in place but turning away in order to learn.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who is busy with his own Torah learning during קריאת התורה is not considered to be forsaking ה׳.

steps.title: Keep up with the weekly portion: text twice, translation once
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר יהודה quotes רבי אמי: a person should always complete his weekly פרשה together with the ציבור, by reading the text twice and the תרגום once.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה said in the name of רבי אמי: A person should always finish his Torah portions along with the congregation. He reads the text twice and the translation once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new teaching about preparing the weekly פרשה. Each person must finish it on his own, keeping pace with the ציבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic is still Torah reading, but the focus moves from how to act in shul to a personal duty. Each week, before the ציבור reads the פרשה, a person reads it himself twice in the original and once in תרגום. The word לעולם shows that this is a steady, regular practice.

keyTerms.meaning: His Torah portions, meaning the weekly פרשה
Together with the congregation, in step with its weekly reading
Twice the Torah text and once the Aramaic translation

steps.whatToRemember: The source for the practice of שנים מקרא ואחד תרגום is רבי אמי, quoted by רב הונא בר יהודה: each week a person completes the פרשה along with the ציבור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis in the גמרא for the well-known halacha of reviewing the weekly פרשה, two times in the text and one time in תרגום.
